questions.question: By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct? × and ÷, 2 and 6 I. 7 – 4 × 3 ÷ 6 + 2 = 8 II. 6 – 8 × 2 + 9 ÷ 3 = 5
questions.questionHtml:
By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?
× and ÷, 2 and 6
I. 7 – 4 × 3 ÷ 6 + 2 = 8
II. 6 – 8 × 2 + 9 ÷ 3 = 5
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Interchanging × and ÷, 2 and 6 in the given equation and find which is not correct.

I. 7 – 4 × 3 ÷ 6 + 2 = 8

After interchanging the sign and numbers we get the:

⇒ 7 – 4 ÷ 3 × 2 + 6 = 8

⇒ 7 - 1.333 × 2 + 6 = 8

⇒ 7 - 2.666 + 6 = 8

⇒ 13 - 2.666 = 8

⇒ 10.334 ≠ 8 (Not correct)

II. 6 – 8 × 2 + 9 ÷ 3 = 5

After interchanging the sign and numbers we get the:

⇒ 2 – 8 ÷ 6 + 9 × 3 = 5

⇒ 2 - 1.333 + 9 × 3 = 5

⇒ 2 - 1.333 + 27 = 5

⇒ 29 - 1.333 = 5

⇒ 27.667 ≠ 5 (Not correct)

So, Both I and II are not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (6) 2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2) 2 = 40
questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

(6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

We have to interchange the two numbers to make the given equation correct.

Let's check the option one by one.

Option 1) 6 and 8

Given : (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ (8)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) × 6} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

⇒ 64 - 20 + 4 - 2 × 6 + 4 = 40

⇒ 64 - 20 + 4 - 12 + 4 = 40

⇒ 72 - 20 - 12 = 40

⇒ 40 = 40 

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 2) 7 and 2

Given : (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 2) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) × 8} \right]\) + (7)2 = 40

⇒ 36 - 20 + 14 - 2 × 8 + 49 = 40

⇒ 36 - 20 + 14 - 16 + 49 = 40

⇒ 99 - 20 - 16 = 40

⇒ 63 ≠ 40

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 2 and 8

Given : (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) × 2} \right]\) + (8)2 = 40

⇒ 36 - 20 + 4 - 2 × 2 + 64 = 40

⇒ 36 - 20 + 4 - 4 + 64 = 40

⇒ 104 - 20 - 4 = 40

⇒ 80 ≠ 40

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) 20 and 8

Given : (6)2 – 20 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) \times 8} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ (6)2 – 8 + (28 ÷ 7) – \(\left[ {\left( {\sqrt 4 } \right) × 20} \right]\) + (2)2 = 40

⇒ 36 - 8 + 4 - 2 × 20 + 4 = 40

⇒ 36 - 8 + 4 - 40 + 4 = 40

⇒ 44 - 8 - 40 = 40

⇒ - 4 ≠ 40

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "6 and 8".

questions.question: Earth’s core is mainly made up of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Earth’s core is mainly made up of ______.
questions.solution: Earth's core is mainly made up of nickel and iron. The innermost layer of the core is solid and made up of nickel and iron, also known as "nife". The outer core is in a liquid state. The core has a very high temperature and pressure and is the innermost layer of the Earth with a radius of about 3500 km. The Earth is divided into four main layers: the solid crust, the mantle, the outer core, and the inner core. The mantle extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust and is the widest section of the Earth.

questions.question: The subject of the Study of Macro Economics is based on which principle?
questions.questionHtml: The subject of the Study of Macro Economics is based on which principle?
questions.solution: The study of macroeconomics is based on the principle of national income. This principle refers to the value of all goods and services produced in a country in a fiscal year, and represents the sum of all economic activity carried out in the country. Macroeconomics examines how economies function, including changes in inflation, interest rates, and economic production, and is critical to achieving poverty alleviation, social equality, and sustainable growth through sound monetary and fiscal policies. Consumer theory and producer theory are fields within microeconomics that investigate how people make choices about spending and how businesses produce goods, respectively.

questions.solution: The correct answer is Article 143, which authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact that are of public importance. Article 142 allows the Supreme Court to pass orders for complete justice, while Article 144 instructs civil and judicial agencies to support the Supreme Court. Article 145 allows the Supreme Court to make rules for regulating its practice and procedure.

R's jogging speed = 5 × 2 ⇒ 10 km/h and R's running speed = 10 × 2 ⇒ 20 km/h

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is unfairly. 

Key Points

  • The context suggests that the leader of the UK’s psychiatrists believes the findings simplifying the issue and attributing young people's mental health problems solely to social media is not entirely justified.
  • The word "unfairly" suggests that social media is being blamed in a way that is not right or just, fitting the context where the psychiatrist feels the conclusions are oversimplified.
  • Words like "legitimately" and "impartially" would imply a sense of fairness or unbiased judgment, which contradicts the leader's perspective that the blame on social media is too simplistic.
  • "Outlandish" would imply something bizarre or extremely unusual, which doesn't fit the context of discussing the validity of blaming social media.
  • The sentence structure and context around blank number 5 indicate the need for an adverb that reflects an opinion on the fairness of the blame placed on social media, making "unfairly" the most appropriate choice.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 3 i.e. unfairly.

Additional Information

  • Legitimately means in a way that conforms to the law or to rules. It doesn't fit the context as the statement is about whether the blame is justified, not whether it's lawful.
  • Impartially means in a way that treats all rivals or disputants equally; fairly. This option doesn't apply because the statement addresses the issue of blame being placed without considering the complexities involved.
  • Outlandish describes something looking or sounding bizarre or unfamiliar. This option is inappropriate because the discussion is about the appropriateness of blame, not the strangeness of the findings.

 

Complete passage: Four of the most popular forms i.e. Facebook, Twitter, Snapchat, and Instagram of social media (1) inflict great damage to young people’s mental health. The findings follow growing (3) concern among politicians, health bodies, doctors, and parents about young people suffering harm as a result of cyberbullying and social media (4) reinforcing feelings of self-loathing and leading them to commit suicide. However, the leader of the UK’s psychiatrists said these findings were too simplistic and they (5) unfairly blamed social media for the complex reasons why the mental health of so many young people is suffering.
